div.p: After that by help of God we hauen iended the furste partie of pis firste book in the whiche it is itreted of mannis owne gouernaunce, schewynge wherinne kynges and princes schullen sette here felicite. For it is not semelich for hem to sette here ende in riches noper in cyuil my3t and strengthe, noper in no suche thinges; but he schal vse al suche thinges, as it is proued tofore atte folle, as instrumentis and inuen[cliones for to come to felicitee. Pei schullen sette here felicite in dede of prudencia, as that dede cometh of charite. For thanne kynges hauen felicite accordyng to here astate, whanne by excityng of [d]eleccioun of God, they rulen hem that bien vnder hem holilyche and rightfulliche by prudencia of regnynge and by lawe of resoun. Thanne the felicite of kynges schal be principalliche iset in God. And by knowyng and loue of hym he schal ordeyne here studie and here lif perto, that bei mowe knowe and loue God and rule the poeple that is vnder ham as verrey Goddes seruauntes by ordre of resoun.

Thanne, for pis is treted, and it is schewed where inne kynges schal sette here ende and felicite by the ordre that is isette, now it is to schewyng in what vertues kynges schal be excellent and vertuous by certeyn hey3tyng and perfeccioun of the soule. Perfore it nedeth firste to schewe whiche bien the vertual poten|cie and my3tes of the soule and in col. 2 whiche my3tes be vertues bien igrounded and ipi3t. And thanne it schal be ischewed how the vertues bien distingued. Perafter we schal declare how many suche vertues ber bien and whiche perof is principale, and whiche is secundary, and thanne we schal trete singulerlich of eueriche of these vertues and how it semeth kynges and princes to haue suche vertues.

The vertual my3tes of the soule mowe be destyngued in these wise: for som bien kynde and natural, and some cognitif and sensitif, and some appetitif, and some intellectual. In natural my3tes of the soule we communeth with herbes and treen, as in vertual my3t of norsching, of wexinge, and of gendrynge, and in suche as corden to herbes and treen. The my3tes of sensitif knowyng and felyng be the si3t, tast, and touche,

and the oper wittes, and berinne we accordeb wip oper bestes. The appetitif is destyngued, for oon appetit is in man and not in oper bestes as the appetit that foloweth the intellectual inwit. And anoper maner appetit is in man and in beste, as the appetite that foloweth the felyng, and suche appetite may be cleped sensualitas. And the appetit that foloweth the intellectual inwit is icleped voluntas, the wille. And in that manere of speche oper bestes hauen the appetite that hatte sensualitas and appetitus sensitiuus, and haueth not the appetite that hatte voluntas, the intellectual wille.

Thanne the vertues of the whiche we thinketh to speke bien goode habites, that is dwellyng places; outhir thai bien in the natural vertual my3tes, oper in the vertual my3tes and wittes of felyng, oper in the appetite sensitif of felyng, oper in | the appetite intellectual, oper in the intellecte and inwyt, oper in al bes, oper in some perof. And a mowe not be in natural vertual mizttes and that is declared in pre wise. [Firste,] for we bep noust preysed nober iblamed for naturel and kynde vertue, for no man is acounted a good man for he hath good degestioun and wexinge. The seconde, suche vertues bep noust in the naturel vertual my3tes, for suche vertues stonden by resoun as it may be preued, ii Ethicorum, and natural my3tes bien not obedient to resoun in that bei bien soche. For bei a man make resouns wheper he wil oper no, properliche for to speke the natural potencial vertues varieth not in here kynde worchynge but wercheth alwey with al here my3t. The pridde, habites and vertues bien not in natural uertual my3tes, for suche habites and vertues inclineth potencial vertues to do wel oper euel, as a vicious habite inclyneth to do euel, and as a vertuous habite inclineth to do wel. Thanne for kynde is inclyned and determined to oon, and potencial vertues bien fol inclyned by kynde to worche by here owne kynde, and so perby we bep noper vertuous ne vicious as we speketh heere of vertueus and of vices; and so perinne may not be suche vertues.

And by the same pre resouns by the whiche it is preued that vertuees bien not in the natural potencial vertues, it may be preued that bei bien not in the knowyng of the fif wittes. For as we ben nou3t ipreysed nober iblamed for natural potencial vertues, so we ben not ipreysed noper iblamed for the fife wittes; for as no man is preysed for a gode man for he hap a gode digestion and wexyng, so man is no3t presed for scharp si3t and gode hiryng, but if it fallep by hap oper yf a man is ble|r ey3ed and his si3t apeired for greet etyng and drynkyng, oper 3if he hath euel digestioun or feblenesse of stomachus for etyng, aliter he schold be blamed for ouer mych drinkyng, aliter, and nou3t for he hath yuel dygestioun, nober for feble si3t ‡‡ - for scharp sight and good digestioun [is not] in oure power propurliche for to speke - but he schulde be blamed fore he hath itake to muche of mete and of drynke, for it was in his powere to ete and drynke mesurableliche.

The secunde, moral vertue is not in the potencial vertue of the fyue wyttes, for as the kynde potencial vertues bep no3t obedient to reson, for by reule of resoun no man hap more digestioun oper lasse, noper more growyng oper lasse: so the fif wittes bien not obedient to resoun, for it is not in manis power to se oper heitlerlich oper dymlich; and 3if moral vertue folweth resoun, thanne vertue is not in fife wittes.

The pridde, moral vertue is not in the fif wittes; for as the natural potencial vertues bep fol set to here worchyng by here owne kynde, so bien the wittes also. For as the fuyre heteth wip al his my3t, for it worcheth by his owne kynde and is berfore noper preysed noper iblamed, noper perinne is moral vertue: so for the potencial vertue of digestioun makep as gret digestioun as he may, and the eyze seeth as moche as he may, perinne may no moral vertue be iset. For by natural vertue, potencial vertue is iset awork atte folle by here owen kynde and nedep berfore no moral vertue. And so moral vertue is not in natural potencial vertue, noper in potencial vertues of the fife wittes; and oper potencial vertues ben pere nou3t bute the intellectualle vertu that is the vnderstondyng and the appetite sensytyue and intellectiue. Thanne | in soche potencial vertues mot be moral vertues.

For it is schewed that moral vertues ben noust in naturel potencial vertues of felyng, now it is to schewyng hou vertues bien distyngwed and how bei bien in the intellectual inwit and in the appetit. Thanne it is to distynguyng of vertues and of suche potencial vertues. For som vertues ben intellectual, and som moral, and somme mene bytwene intellectual and moral.

The intellectual vertues bien in the inwit that hatte intellectus speculatiuus, that is the schewyng of the inwit, and soche vertues bien speculatif sciens, as natural philosophi, gemetrie, and methaphisik, and oper suche. And pure moral vertues bien in the appetite sensitif oper intellectif. And soche vertues bien iusticia, temporancia, fortitudo, mansuetudo and oper soche, of the whiche we schal trete syngulerlich. The mene vertues bytwene intellectual and moral bep in the inwyt, that hatte intellectus practicus, as prudencia and opere vertues that longep thereto. The comentor super libris Ethicorum seith that prudencia is acounted a mene vertue bytwene moral vertues and intellectual vertues and may natheles be accounted with moral vertues. But prudencia is not but in goode men as morel vertues beth not bote in gode men. Schrewed men, bei3 bei mowe be kunnynge, falce and gylefole, bei mowe not be prudentes, as it schal be declared in the place perof. Perfore, vi Ethicorum, it is iseid that it is inpossible to be prudens and not good.

Thanne we leuep the vertues intellectual and sciens speculatif and schal trete of prudencia and of moral vertues. For as we hauen ofte seyd, we taken this werk not for to be kunnynge | bote for to be good, for goodnesse may not be in vs withoute prudencia and moral vertues.

5 These vertues may be in the inwit, that hatte intellectus, that is to say vnderstondyng, and in the appetite also. And it is seid that a vertue is som what after resoun. Thanne the vertue moot be in the resonable vertue and potencial my3t. And the philosofer setteth double resonable, oon by his owne essencia, and an oper by that he is partener of resoun. The vnderstondyng and the inwit that hatte intellectus is resonable by his owne essencia and by itself. And the appetit is resonable by that he is partiner of resoun. For beiz the appetit is not intellectus and the silf resoun, zit he is aconted partiner of resoun, for he may be obedient to resoun. The natural potencial vertues and the fif wittes of felyng ben not resonable of hemself, nor bei bien not the silue resoun resoun and bei bien not parteners of resoun nor sogette to resoun in so moche as bei bien potencial vertues. Thanne in the fif wittes and in the natural potencial vertues bien not moral vertues, as it is iseide tofore honde; but bei bien oonlich in the inwit and vnderstondyng, that hatte intellectus, and in the appetite.

And in vs is double knowyng, intellectif and sensitif. For as kynde appetite folweth kyndelich the forme that a hath by kynde, so the appetit of knowyng folweth the forme that apprehendep and conceyueth by knowyng. For as heuy thinges, for bei hauen the fourme of heuynesse, bei hauen also a certeyne kynde inclynacioun and kynde appetit to desire to be bynethe and lowe, so bei that hauen knowyng, in that bei hauen in hemself the fourme that is conceyued, bei hauen also som inclinacioun and some appetit as that fourme mouep.

Perfore as we hauen double knowyng, | sencitif and intellectif, so we this hauen doble appetit; sencitif that folwep the fourme that is conceyued by the wit of felyng, and intellectif that is the forme that is conceyued by the vnderstondyng, that hatte intellectus. And the appetit sencitif is double. For bestes bien aboue soules bynges and kynde zeueth double potencial vertue to elementis and to soules bynges, oon by the whiche bei desiren here owne reste and anoper by the whiche bei withstonden bynges that lettep and bien contrary, moche more kynde i3euep to bestes double potencial vertue, for bei bien more parfit thanne soules bynges. We seep that fuyre is hoot and li3t by kynde, and by li3tnesse desireth his owne place and quyete accordyng thereto, and worchep by hete and withstondep thynges that bien contrarie thereto. Thanne for fuyre schulde not be ilet by contrarie byngys to reste by li3tnesse in his owne place, kynde zeueth thereto potencial vertue to hete that it may perby worche and withstonde pinges that ben contrarie and corumpep fyre. Thanne 3if kynde zeueth to fyre and to soules bynges double potencial

vertue, oon by the whiche he geteth here owne quiete and reste, and anoper by the whiche he worcheb and withstondep lettes and contrarie bynges, moche more kynde ijeuep to bestes suche potencial vertues. Thanne kynde jeuep to hem double appetit, sencitif appetite of felyng, oon by the whiche a pursewep and cometh to here owne quiete and likynge, and this potencial vertue concupiscibilis he hizte, that is coueitisnesse; and anoper by the whiche he withstondep and resłep contrarie and lettes, and that hatte irascibilis, as it were potencial wrep. So that the concupiscible is as it were in stede of listnesse and heuynesse in list bynges and heuy. The irascibilis is as it were in stede of cold and of hete in colde | bynges and hote. For as heuye bynges by heuynesse forsakep the ouer place as not accordynge and cometh to be nether place as conuenient and accordyng, and wibstondep by cold bynges that bien contrarie and letteb and sauep hemself that they bien not corrupt in here kynde, noper ilet of here owne place and quiete; so by the concupiscibilis, bestes voyden and forsaken yuel bynges and displesynge, and folwep and takep goode bynges and likynge. And by irascibilis a reseth and puttep of and wipstandep the contrarie that myzt hem lette of suche likynge oper of plesance. By the concupiscibilis he goop and comep and takep mete as byng that is conuenient and accordyng and likynge. And by the irascibilis a resep and withstondep oper that lettep hem of here mete.

Perfore it is wel seid that the concupiscibilis takep hede to good and to iuel for bei bien soche, and the irascibilis takep hede to good and to iuel in so moche as bei bien hard to voide opere to come to. For good is desired for it is good, and yuel is schoned and forsake for it is euyl. The concupiscibilis is inclined and desireth reste and pyng that is good and likynge, and schonep and forsakep euel bynges and vnlikyng, and hath for obiecte sensible goode and euel for bei bien soche (that is to menyng al that is desired or schoned and forsake is good oper euel, sensible in that that bei bien sensible). By the irascible we reseth and withstondep in that wyse bynges that greuep vs and lettep. And the irascibiles, that is wretheful doyng, longep to good and yuel, not onlich for pey bien suche, bote for bei bien gete or kept oper withstonde with hard diffecultee. For hard difficultee lettep vs principalliche to gete good and voyde yuel and harme. Thanne kynde rulede vnparfitliche jif he jaf to bestes the concupiscibel to desire good and to schone and forsake yuel, but jif he jaf to hem also | the irascibel by the whiche a reseth and defendep and wibstondep greues and lettes that lettep hem of delectacion and likyng. Thanne for bestes scholde haue ful lykynge by the concupiscible in manere that is accordyng to hem, the irascibel is ijeue to hem by the whiche a reseth and wibstondep bynges that greueth and lettep hem of delectacioun and likyng. Thanne the appetite sencitif of felyng is double, irascible and concupiscible.

For it is not inow to wite and to knowe whaat manere byng is wedloc and how a man scholde haue hymself in wyuynge but he knowe also how he schulde bere hymself to his wif he is iwedded, perfore to be forseide chapitres resonabeliche this processe is annexed that we may knowe how rewlyng of wedloc by the whiche wyues ben irewled is distyngwed fro other manere rewlyng. And by twey weyes we may declare that wifes and children ben irewled by diuers manere of reulyng. The firste wey is itake by the manere of reulynge, and the seconde, by worchyng and doyng.

The firste is declared in this wise. For philosofres menen that the manere reulyng of the world is ikept and isaued in oon man, perfore among hem man is icleped the lasse world. For as al the worlde is rewled by oon prince and by oon God that is vnderstondyng, intellecte seuered and pured and not bodiliche, so ⌜al⌝⌝pat⌝┌al┐┐pat┐ is in a man, jif he scholde be rewled bewliche, is rewled by intellecte (vnderstondyng) and resoun; so that the manere | of rewelyng of the world is ikepte and isaued in eche man, so that Plato sauede al the ordere of heuenes in eche resonable soule. Thanne jif the rewelyng of the world is likned to the rewelyng that scholde be in o ‡‡ man, and a cyte is a partie of the worlde, thanne the rewelyng of an hool cytee scholde be more ikepte and isaued in oon hous. For jif an hous is more than oon synguler man and a cyte lasse than the world, jif the liknesse of the hool world is ikepte and isaued in oon man, moche more the liknesse of the rewlyng of a cyte is ikept and isaued in oon hous. Perfore, primo Poleticorum, the philosofer liknep the rewlyng of oon hous to the reulyng of a cyte. And as it longeth to this doynge, a cyte may be reuled by double manere rewlyng: by politik rewlyng and by real rewlyng.

And he is lord by real lordschipe that is lord and rewleth by avisement and by lawes that he makeb and zeuep and not by lawes that citeseyns makep. And whan a prince in a cyte is prince and lord and makep lawys and rewlep perby that rewlyng hap the name of prince oper kyng and is icleped real rewlyng.

But whan nober prince ne kyng makep the lawe but the citeseyns, thanne rewlyng by that lawe hap not the name of kyng noper of prince noper is icleped real rewlyng but it hath the name of policye, the comynte and of citeseyns, and is icleped politik rewelyng oper cyuyle rewelyng.

And in Poleticis, to these twey manere of rewlyng in a cyte the philosofer likneth twey manere reulynges of on hous by the whiche the fader | rewleth the child and the housebonde the wif. For the rewlyng paternale by the whiche the fader reuleth the child is ilikned to real rewelyng, and the rewlyng coniugale by the whiche the housebonde scholde rewle the wif as it is ilikned to politikrewelyng. For the housebond schulde be aboue the wif and rewle here by politik rewelyng, for he schuld rewle here certeyn as by lawe of wedlok and matrimoyne and by condiciouns and couenantes. But the fader scholde rewle the child by auysement and as hym likep and by real rewlyng, for betweyne the fader and the childe is no couenant imaad how he scholde be rewled. But the fader gouerneth and rewleth his child as hym liketh and as hym semep that it is best and most spedfol for the child as a kyng scholde rewle his men frelich as hym semep it is best and most spedful for the men. Wherfore suche rewlyng is icleped real rewlyng. But alwey bytwene housebonde and wif is som forward and couenant and som wordes ispoke how the housebond scholde bere hym to his wif. And perfore suche rewlyng is icleped politik rewelyng, for it is ilikned to that rewlyng by the whiche citeseyns clepen here lord and schewen to hym charters and dedes and couenantes that he scholde holde in his rewlyng.

Thanne by the manere of rewlyng it is declared how the oon is politik and the other real and how the rewlyng paternale, faderlich, by the whiche the fader rewleth the child and the rewlyng coniugale by the which the housebond reulep the wif ben diuerce. F F For we seen that real rewelyng is TfTf ful and hole and kynde rewelyng, and politik rewelyng is 11 parcial rewelyng and by eleccioun. For he that rewelep realliche hap ful and hole rewelyng and fre, and he that rewlep pollitiklich hap not ful and hool rewelyng nober symple withoute condicioun but bi certeyn condiciouns and couenantes. Also bei eche | riztful rewlyng be kynde rewlyng, zut politik rewlyng be it neuere so riztfol it is not so kynde rewelyng as ryal reulyng, for that rewlyng comep in som wise by eleccioun for in suche reulynge cyteseyns chesen hem a lord.

Herby the dyuersite is iknowe betweyne rewlyng paternale by the whiche the fader rewleth the child and the rewlyng nupciale by the whiche the housebonde rewlep the wif, for the fader hap more maystrie and more hool and ful rewlyng of the child thanne the housebonde of the wif. Also the fadres lordschipe of the child is more kynde lordschipe thanne the housebondes lordschipe ouer the wif, for in som wise the wif is acounted pere to the housebonde and cheseth here an housebonde. And children ben not icounted peres to the fader nober cheseb hem a fader but bei ben kyndeliche igendred and comeb of the fader. Thanne pe lordschipe paternale that the fader hab of oon child is more kyndelich than the lordschip coniugale that the housebond hab of the wif. For beiz a man be kyndelich desposed to wedloc, gif that he hab this womman or thulke to wyf is at his owne wille and free eleccioun. So as a man is kyndelich ydowede to spekyng, beiz he speke this proper langage ober that, it is at his owne wille and free eleccioun. Thanne the rewelyng coniugale is not so kyndelich as the rewlyng paternale, for in no wise children chesen hem a fader.

It is iknowe how rewelyng coniugale and the rewelyng paternale ben diuerse by the manere of rewlyng, for the oon is more symple and kyndelich and the other is more parciale and by eleccioun; it may be sone iknowe how this twey manere of rewlyng ben diuerse by workes and dedes. For the fader scholde so rewle the children that he scholde ordeyne hem to other workes and dedes than his wif, for children scholde lerne workys and dedes of cheualrye | and of cyuel and dure col. 2 suche workes and dedes whan bey ben of age and wyues scholde not lerne suche workes and dedes for he schulde not vse suche workes and dedes.
Thanne it is iknowe that alle citeseins scholde reule here wifes and children by dyuerse manere rewlyng but that is most semelich for kynges and princes for bei scholde keepe and holde kynde resoun.

It was iseid tofore that in an hous ben diuerse maneres of rewlyng: the rewlyng nupciale by the whiche the housebonde rewleth the wif, the rewlyng paternal by the whiche the fader rewleb the child, and the rewlyng domynatiuum that is lordes rewle by the whiche a lord rewlep his seruantes. Thanne after, we hauen distyngwed bytwene rewlynges coniugale, that is rewlyng of wedloc, and paternale, that is fader rewlyng, for paternale is more ful and hool rewlyng and symple withoute condicioun, and the rewlyng nupciale is parciale. And for the paternale rewlyng is more kyndelich and the nupciale rewlyng is in som wise by eleccioun, also for wif and seruant ben iordeyned to dyuerse workes and dedes, it is to declarynge how the wif and seruant scholde be diuersliche irewled. And that a man scholde not bylede his wif as a seruant we may preue by pre weyes: the firste is itake by kynde ordre, the seconde by perfeccioun of hous, the pridde by that the housebonde and wif ben peres.

The firste mene is declared in this wise. For al the hool kynde is imeued and irewled by God and by angelis; and as the philosofre seith in libro De Fortuna, the kynde inclynacioun and excityng that we hauen in the soule we hauen of God as of hym that meuep | al the hole kynde. Thanne as in a crafty work that is imaad and iwro3t by a wis crafty worchere is not ifounde to moche ne to lyte, so kynde, but it be ylette, worchep not to moche noper dop superfluyte noper faillep in nedful thinges and necessarie. For kynde is imeued and irewled by the most wis crafty worchere that is God. Thanne al pyng that kynde makep and ordeyneth moot be moost ordenate, for he rewleth kynde of the whiche al ordre comep.

Thanne for a thing is best iordeyned and most ordynate whan oon is iordeyned to oon office, for the wif is kyndeliche iordeyned for gendryng and getyng of children, thanne he schal not be iordeyned to seruyng. Perfore it is iseide, primo Poleticorum, that wif and seruant ben kyndelich distingwed and dyuerse; for as he seith there, kynde dop no thyng noper makep as smepis maade a swerd Delficus for suche men. For among Delphes were swerdes imaad for poore men so that oon swerd seruede to many office, as pore men that my3te not haue many instru20 mentes lette make oon instrument that my3te serue in many offis. But kynde dop not soo; but for kynde thinges scholde be the bettre, alwey on thing is iordeyned to oon offis. Perfore the philosofre seith that eche instrument dop best his work 3 if it serueth not to many workes and dyuerse but onlich to oon. Wherfore for kynde ordeyneth the wif to conseyuyng and to beryng of children, it were vnsemelich that sche were iordeyned to seruynge. Thanne it were not kynde ordre 3 if the housebond rewled the wif by the same manere rewlyng | by the whiche a col. 2 lord rewleth his seruantes.

But pei3 it be in this wise by kynde ordre, 3 it among som men and nacions, among barbares and stronge men, the wif is seruant, as the philosofer seith, i Poleticorum, and seith that among barbaros and stronge men, wif and seruant hauen the same ordre for bei vsed here wifes as seruantes. But that was, as it is iseid there, for among suche barbares rr is no kyndelich prince; but swiche barbares TT ben kyndelich straunge and seruant, for he is barbarus that is strange to a man TT and ‡‡ is not vnderstonde of hym, for a man is barbarus to anoper for the other vnderstondep hym not. And so a Duchesch man is barbarus to an Italian and a Italian is barbarus to an Englische man. And he is sympathiche barbarus withoute condicioun that is strange to hymself and woot not what he hymself meneth; but that may not be but hym lacke vnderstondyng and vse of reson. And for he that lackep vse of resoun is kyndelich a seruant for he can not rewle hymself, it is spedful to hym to be rewled of som other. He that is barbarus by kynde is seruant be kynde. Wherfore 3 if among the barbarus wif and seruant haue the same
ordre, that is for defaute of reson; for they kunne not distyngwe bytwene the manere of rewelyng of wif and of seruant.

Wherfore 3if it is semelich that alle citeseyns be wise and redy and knowe the kynde manere and ordre, it is vnsemelich to hem to vse here wyfes as seruantes. Bot that is more vnsemelich for kynges and princes, for it is more vnsemelich that bei ben barbarus and lacke wit and resoun. Thanne by kynde ordre it is declared that rewlyng coniugale and rewlyng seruyle ben diuerse and that wifes scholde not be ivsed as seruantes; by rewlyng coniugale the housebonde rewlep the wif and | f. 78f by rewlyng seruyle the lord rewleth his seruantes.

The seconde wey to preue the same is itake by perfeccioun of hous. For an hous semeth vnparfit wip scarsete of thinges and not suffisaunt to hitself in leuynge 3if wif and seruant hauen the same ordre. Perfore it is iseid, vi Poleticorum, that pore men, for pei hauen not many seruantes noper plente of thinges that nedep to the perfeccioun of an hous, bei vsen here wifes and children as it were seruantes.

The pridde mene is itake by that the housebonde and wif ben peres. For bei the housebonde be aboue the wif, he can more resoun; zit he scholde not be so moche aboue here that he scholde vse here as a seruant but as a felawe. For the housebonde is not so moche aboue the wif as the lord is aboue the seruant, but the housebonde and wif ben acounted peres in som wise.
